images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of EmbodiedLab.Thirty quantitative experiments in five disciplines ask the agent to measure, predict or configure a system drawn anew per instance, by changing its state and reading the feedback on the instruments. Agents are ranked by their success rate at the lowest interface level, T0, and also evaluated at T1; the diagnostic level T2 and four capability dimensions serve the analysis.

Figure 2:Acting to know.(a) Manipulation benchmarks stop at acting to change the scene into a named target state; science benchmarks find things out without physical action. (b) Given a goal, a EmbodiedLab agent changes the state of the apparatus through interaction, observes the feedback and acts again on what it learned, in the same loop across disciplines; at submission, what it found out, the evidence it recorded and the bench state are scored.

Figure 3:One episode on the lens experiment.(a) A hiddenθ\thetafixes the system; the task card gives the objective, public parameters and rules, but no method. (b) The agent acts and observes through three cameras while the environment keeps a record. (c) Success requires every gate and an error within tolerance of the hidden target.

Figure 4:Interface levels.Robot, bench and camera views are the same at every level; each level supplies more between the agent and the robot. (a) T0 supplies only the camera images, the robot state, joint position targets and gripper commands. (b) T1 supplies ground-truth depth on segmentation masks and cuRobo[41]planning against the true obstacles, shown with real outputs of T1 runs. (c) T2 adds a skill library, distilled from the successful runs of the strongest agents, in the agent’s workspace.

Figure 5:Construction pipeline, illustrated with the cantilever experiment. Every experiment passes five stages before release; a defect found at any stage is fixed in the bench and the affected stages run again. The validation data are inFig.8.
Figure 7:Overview of the 30 experiments, grouped by primary capability dimension, as seen by one of the robot’s fixed cameras during a reference run. The tag gives the tier.

Figure 10:Why runs fail at T0.(a) Failed runs by the cause of their first decisive error, in percent of each agent’s failed runs with an attributed cause, grouped by the stage of acting to know. (b) Typical failures, five per stage, each shown in a frame from the agent’s own cameras with the decisive spot ringed; the chip on each frame names the cause.
